metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic on the specific trials where Tallying and WADD make diametrically opposed predictions. In Trial 1 and Trial 2, one option has a higher count of winning features (favored by Tallying), while the other option has a higher validity-weighted sum (favored by WADD). Tallying models will score close to 1.0, whereas WADD models will score close to 0.0, maximizing discrimination.

In the specific trial where option A has the two most valid cues and option B has the three least valid cues, the WADD theory predicts a preference for option A because the sum of the highest validities outweighs the sum of the lowest. Conversely, the Tallying heuristic predicts a preference for option B because it has more positive cues in total. Measuring the proportion of times option B is chosen on this specific trial robustly discriminates the two theories.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices consistent with Tallying on the critical 'mismatch' trials where Tallying and WADD strongly disagree. For example, when Option A has more winning features but Option B has the highest-validity features, Tallying prefers A while WADD prefers B. This targeted proportion will be much higher under Tallying than under WADD.

This metric isolates trials where the two options are [1, 1, 0, 0, 0] and [0, 0, 1, 1, 1]. In these trials, the WADD model generally prefers the option with two highly valid features (the first two), because their combined subjective weight outweighs the three less valid features. In contrast, the Tallying heuristic strictly counts the number of features won and strongly prefers the option with three winning features over the one with two. By computing the proportion of times the subject chooses the option with fewer but higher-validity features, we expect a high value under WADD and a low value under Tallying.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the strictly non-compensatory Take-The-Best (TTB) heuristic. Because the experimental design contains many trials where the single most valid feature is contradicted by the sum of the remaining features, TTB and WADD yield opposing predictions on these trials. TTB simulates will consistently produce a high proportion of TTB-aligned choices (limited only by noise), while WADD simulates (which are compensatory for most of the gamma parameter space) will frequently choose the option favored by the lower-validity cues, resulting in a significantly lower TTB-alignment score.

This metric calculates the probability of choosing Option B on 'compensatory' trials. These are trials specifically designed so that the highest-validity discriminating feature favors Option B (which Take-The-Best will strictly follow, predicting a response near 1.0), but the sheer number of remaining lower-validity features favors Option A (which Weighted Additive will integrate, predicting a response near 0.0). By restricting the analysis only to these critical trials, we achieve maximal separation between the two theories.
